name: שִׂרְיֹן
summary: Sirion is the Sidonian name for Mount Hermon. Psalm 29 pairs it with Lebanon and pictures the mountains leaping at Yahweh’s voice. The text gives no derivation of the name.

evidence.note: Sirion leaps like a young wild ox at Yahweh’s voice.
“The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.”

note: Moved from the former word entry `cireyon` (old root key שׂרינ). TIPNR files Sirion under Hermon_Mount@Deu.3.8. The geographical name has no final tet. The incision words indexed nearby belong to שׂרט. Deuteronomy 3:9 distinguishes Sirion from the Amorite name Senir.
